title: Define the API contract
why: Inputs and failures must have predictable behavior.
dataset: Valid, invalid, absent, empty and unauthorized request cases.
metric: Schema validity, expected error types and authorization outcomes.
evidence: Versioned contract tests; explicit timeout and retry behavior.
decision: Which callers and tenants may access which resources?

title: Establish the source of the data
why: Retrieval and training inherit source errors and access limits.
dataset: Representative documents, formats, access labels and deletion cases.
metric: Parse accuracy, source coverage and access-control violations.
evidence: Document lineage, licensed use, retention and corpus version.
decision: What may leave the boundary, and what must be removed?

title: Build a retrieval golden dataset
why: An answer cannot cite evidence it never retrieved.
dataset: Realistic questions with reviewed relevant passage IDs, including no-answer and difficult slices.
metric: Recall@k, hit@k, ranking quality and latency at a fixed k.
evidence: Frozen corpus, labeled relevance, baseline and held-out results.
decision: What counts as sufficient evidence for each question?

title: Evaluate the answer against evidence
why: Plausible language and valid citations do not prove support.
dataset: Questions, trusted sources, answer rubrics and unanswerable cases.
metric: Task success, supported claims, omissions and correct abstention.
evidence: Human-reviewed rubrics and output/source pairs by risk slice.
decision: Which unsupported claim could cause harm?

title: Test the tool and permission boundary
why: A tool call can change real state.
dataset: Authorized and denied actions, injection attempts, cancellation, stale state and duplicate requests.
metric: Invariant violations, task completion and incorrect side effects.
evidence: Recorded tool arguments, permission decisions and state assertions.
decision: Which actions require a person, and who may approve them?

title: Calibrate automated evaluators
why: An evaluator can agree with itself and still be wrong.
dataset: Independent human labels, borderline cases and disagreement examples.
metric: Agreement, per-class precision/recall and systematic judge bias.
evidence: Rubric version, calibration set and adjudication record.
decision: When do people review disagreement or low confidence?

title: Compare changes with uncertainty
why: A small observed improvement can be noise.
dataset: Paired cases from a held-out set, representative slices and repeat runs where needed.
metric: Paired differences, suitable confidence intervals and practical effect size.
evidence: Predeclared decision rule, sample unit and uncertainty analysis.
decision: What improvement matters, and how costly is a false win?

title: Connect quality to operations
why: A service needs both dependable operation and useful outputs.
dataset: Expected load, failures, canary traffic and sampled production cases.
metric: Error rates, tail latency, cost, task quality and drift.
evidence: Minimized traces, alert ownership, runbook and rollback proof.
decision: What triggers rollback, and which content may telemetry retain?

title: Validate model-serving capacity
why: A model that fits in memory may still miss the service target.
dataset: Representative prompt lengths, concurrency and burst workloads.
metric: Time to first token, tokens/s, tail latency, memory and task quality.
evidence: Load-test configuration, model/license provenance and capacity limits.
decision: Which quantization and batching choices preserve quality?

title: Protect the adaptation holdout
why: Optimization can learn quirks of your metric or dataset.
dataset: Separate train, development and independent test sets split by entity or time where needed.
metric: Held-out task success, regressions, leakage and safety slices.
evidence: Dataset lineage, experiment configuration and comparison to the base system.
decision: Why should prompt optimization or training beat the simpler baseline?

title: Review synthetic data before use
why: Generated examples can repeat errors and hide missing cases.
dataset: Labeled source of each synthetic case, deduplication and independently collected examples.
metric: Diversity, review error rate, leakage and real-data performance.
evidence: Generator version, human review and separation from evaluation gold.
decision: Which real cases are missing from the synthetic distribution?
